candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — occupied-bed linen change
candidate.educational_objective: Use the occupied-bed technique to change linens safely for a client who must remain in bed while preserving privacy, comfort, and safe repositioning.

options.A: Use an occupied-bed technique, turning the client safely from side to side while changing one half of the bed at a time and maintaining coverage and privacy.
options.B: Postpone linen changes until the client can stand independently even when the linens are soiled.
options.C: Remove all linens first and leave the client uncovered while the replacement linens are prepared.
options.D: Have the immobile client stand briefly at the bedside so the linens can be changed more quickly.

candidate.rationale: NCBI Nursing Assistant guidance provides an occupied-bed checklist for clients who remain in bed. The technique uses safe side-to-side rolling while soiled linens are rolled inward and clean linens are placed on one side and then pulled through after the client is turned. Privacy, coverage, safe handling, and post-procedure safety are maintained throughout. A is therefore correct; B through D unnecessarily delay care or create privacy and fall/injury risks.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For a client who remains in bed, an occupied-bed technique changes linens by safely rolling the client from side to side while maintaining coverage, privacy, and safety.
